title: Dinaturality of the system projection-evaluation word
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$, uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$, $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For every scheme $W$ use a small skeleton of $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$, completed coefficient sheaf $R_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$, and ordinary unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. On the vertical sequence site write $\mathcal Q_W(n,U)=(A_n)_W(U)$, $R_W^{\mathrm{const}}$ for the constant sequence ring, $\mathscr P$ for the one-point sequence topos, and $\mathcal A=(A_n)_n$ for its quotient ring [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site]. Let $\rho_W:(W^{\mathrm{Tow}},\mathcal Q_W)\to(W^{\mathrm{Tow}},R_W^{\mathrm{const}})$ and $\rho_0:(\mathscr P,\mathcal A)\to(\mathscr P,R)$ be scalar restriction morphisms. Write $g_W^{\mathcal Q}$ and $g_W^R$ for point-sections morphisms to these one-point sequence topoi, with $g_W^R\rho_W=\rho_0g_W^{\mathcal Q}$. The symbol $Rg_*$ means derived sections with values in towers, without inverse limit. Restriction $\rho_*$ is exact. Use the derived internal Hom and signed closed tensor-Hom structure [def-pur-derived-internal-hom, def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model].
Let $k$ be a field with $\ell$ invertible, and let $a:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism between finite-type $k$-schemes, with a fixed compactification $X\xrightarrow j Z\xrightarrow pY$, $pj=a$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. On the quotient sequence sites put $F^{\mathcal Q}=Rp_*^{\mathcal Q}j_!$, with proper image derived after exact open extension, and $F_n=Rp_{*,n}j_!$ at $A_n$ [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. For $K\in D(R_X)$ put $V=\operatorname{const}K$ and $M=L\rho_X^*V$, with $M_n=K_n=K\otimes^L_{R_X}(A_n)_X$ and actual quotient transitions [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction].
For arbitrary $U,N\in D(\mathcal Q_X)$ put $h(U,N)=Rg_{X*}^{\mathcal Q}R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal Q_X}(U,N)$, $b_U=Rg_{Y*}^{\mathcal Q}F^{\mathcal Q}U$, $B_U=\rho_{0*}b_U$. Let $\widetilde\beta_{U,N}:\rho_{0*}h(U,N)\otimes_R^LB_U\to B_N$ be the specified projection-evaluation word of [lem-coef-system-projection-evaluation]: scalar restriction balancing, symmetry, the sections projection mate, the proper projection mate, the open tensor comparison, and $F^{\mathcal Q}$ of closed evaluation after the source-sections counit. For every $u:U\to U'$ and $v:N\to N'$ it satisfies
$$\widetilde\beta_{U,N}\circ(\rho_{0*}h(u,N)\otimes1_{B_U})=\widetilde\beta_{U',N}\circ(1_{\rho_{0*}h(U',N)}\otimes B(u)),$$
$$B(v)\circ\widetilde\beta_{U,N}=\widetilde\beta_{U,N'}\circ(\rho_{0*}h(U,v)\otimes1_{B_U}).$$
The first equality has source $\rho_{0*}h(U',N)\otimes_R^LB_U$. Both are identities in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(R)))$. Their normalization before compact support is closed dinaturality
$$\operatorname{ev}_{U,N}\circ(1_U\otimes R\mathcal Hom(u,N))=\operatorname{ev}_{U',N}\circ(u\otimes1)$$
on $U\otimes^LR\mathcal Hom(U',N)$, with the canonical graded symmetry. The corresponding identity after the $g_X$ counit is on $U\otimes^LLa^*Lg_Y^*h(U',N)$; the open tensor comparison and the natural projection mates for $p,g_Y,\rho_0$ carry it to the displayed whole-system identities. For any $K,K'\in D(R_X)$ and $f:K\to K'$, with $U=M(K)$, $U'=M(K')$ and $u=M(f)$, the canonical natural full-system Hom comparisons of [lem-coef-hom-tower-scalar-model] carry the first equality to $\beta_{K,N}(\mathsf H_N(f)\otimes1)=\beta_{K',N}(1\otimes B(f))$. There is no trace or inverse limit in these identities, and equality of system morphisms is not inferred from finite evaluations.

proof.text:
Use the evaluation convention of [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model], writing $D_{U,N}=R\mathcal Hom(U,N)$ and $e_{U,N}:U\otimes^LD_{U,N}\to N$. Naturality of the closed adjunction in its tensor parameter, evaluated on the identity of $D_{U',N}$, gives
$$e_{U,N}(1\otimes D(u,N))=e_{U',N}(u\otimes1).$$
Indeed both sides transpose to $D(u,N):D_{U',N}\to D_{U,N}$. Naturality of its counit in the target gives
$$v e_{U,N}=e_{U,N'}(1\otimes D(U,v)).$$
If evaluation is first written with the Hom factor on the left, insert the prescribed graded symmetry on both sides; its naturality gives exactly these same formulas. All arrows $u,v$ have degree zero, so this introduces no additional sign.

source.place: Tag 08J9, sites-cohomology-lemma-internal-hom; formal consequences of the recorded closed adjunction

proof.text:
In the word of [lem-coef-system-projection-evaluation], abbreviate $S=Rg_{X*}^{\mathcal Q}$, $T=Rg_{Y*}^{\mathcal Q}$, $F=F^{\mathcal Q}$, $s=Lg_Y^{\mathcal Q*}$, and $t=La^{\mathcal Q*}s\cong Lg_X^{\mathcal Q*}$. Put $h_{U,N}=SD_{U,N}$. For any $d:D\to D'$ the natural counit of the derived adjunction in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], applied to $g_X^{\mathcal Q}$, satisfies
$$d\varepsilon_D=\varepsilon_{D'}t(Sd).$$
Thus the prescribed $v_{U,N}=e_{U,N}(1\otimes\varepsilon_{D_{U,N}})$ obeys, by substitution in step 1,
$$v_{U,N}(1\otimes t h(u,N))=v_{U',N}(u\otimes1),\qquad v v_{U,N}=v_{U,N'}(1\otimes t h(U,v)).$$
The source of the first identity is $U\otimes^Lt h_{U',N}$, as required. Pullback composition is the same natural identification as in the specified word.

source.place: Tag 07A6, sites-cohomology-lemma-adjoint; naturality of the derived adjunction counit

proof.text:
The projection mates of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] are natural in both their arguments on the unbounded derived categories of the small ringed sequence sites. The open comparison $\gamma$ of [lem-coef-support-open-tensor-model] is likewise natural in both arguments on these sites. Consequently the specific composite $\Pi$ of [lem-coef-system-projection-evaluation] satisfies, for $w:U\to U'$ and $\lambda:L\to L'$,
$$F(w\otimes La^*\lambda)\Pi_{U,L}=\Pi_{U',L'}(F(w)\otimes\lambda).$$
To check the composite, move $F(w)\otimes\lambda$ through $\pi_p$ using its two-variable naturality and then through $Rp_*(\gamma)$ using that of $\gamma$; functoriality of $Rp_*$ gives the displayed equality. Here $L,L'$ are arbitrary: this uses neither a projection isomorphism nor a finite-Tor hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0B56, sites-cohomology-equation-projection-formula-map; naturality of the specified projection mate and open comparison

proof.text:
For a tower coefficient object $H\in D(\mathcal A)$ set
$$r_{U,H}=T(\Pi_{U,sH})\pi_{g_Y;FU,H}:b_U\otimes_{\mathcal A}^LH\longrightarrow TF(U\otimes^LtH).$$
Naturality of $\pi_{g_Y}$ from [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], followed by step 3, yields
$$TF(w\otimes t z)r_{U,H}=r_{U',H'}(b(w)\otimes z)$$
for $z:H\to H'$. The actual word of [lem-coef-system-projection-evaluation] is $q_{U,N}=TF(v_{U,N})r_{U,h_{U,N}}$. Taking $z=h(u,N)$ and then $w=u$, steps 2 and the displayed identity give
$$q_{U,N}(1\otimes h(u,N))=TF(v_{U,N}(1\otimes t h(u,N)))r_{U,h_{U',N}}=q_{U',N}(b(u)\otimes1).$$
Similarly take $z=h(U,v)$; functoriality and the second identity of step 2 give
$$b(v)q_{U,N}=q_{U,N'}(1\otimes h(U,v)).$$

source.place: Tag 0B56, sites-cohomology-equation-projection-formula-map; composition of its naturality squares

proof.text:
Write $\rho=\rho_{0*}$ and $l=L\rho_0^*$. The prescribed scalar map in [lem-coef-system-projection-evaluation] is $c_{H,B}=\rho(1\otimes\varepsilon_B)\pi_{\rho_0;H,\rho B}$. For $x:H\to H'$ and $y:B\to B'$, naturality of $\pi_{\rho_0}$ in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] and the counit identity $\varepsilon_{B'}l(\rho y)=y\varepsilon_B$ give
$$c_{H',B'}(\rho x\otimes_R^L\rho y)=\rho(x\otimes_{\mathcal A}^Ly)c_{H,B}.$$
Explicitly the left side becomes $\rho((1\otimes\varepsilon_{B'})(x\otimes l\rho y))\pi_{\rho_0;H,\rho B}$; substitute the counit identity and factor out $\rho(x\otimes y)$. Naturality of the prescribed symmetry also gives $\sigma_{H',B'}(x\otimes y)=(y\otimes x)\sigma_{H,B}$.

source.place: Tag 0B56, sites-cohomology-equation-projection-formula-map, with the adjunction counit of Tag 07A6

proof.text:
Now expand the specified word $\widetilde\beta_{U,N}=\rho(q_{U,N}\sigma_{h_{U,N},b_U})c_{h_{U,N},b_U}$. Step 5 first moves $\rho h(u,N)\otimes1$ through $c$ and $\sigma$, leaving
$$\rho\bigl(q_{U,N}(1\otimes h(u,N))\sigma_{h_{U',N},b_U}\bigr)c_{h_{U',N},b_U}.$$
Substitute step 4 and move $b(u)$ back through the symmetry and $c$ by step 5. This is $\widetilde\beta_{U',N}(1\otimes\rho b(u))$, the first required equality. For the second equality, insert $\rho b(v)$ after this same word, use $b(v)q_{U,N}=q_{U,N'}(1\otimes h(U,v))$ from step 4, and move $h(U,v)$ through the symmetry and $c$. The result is $\widetilde\beta_{U,N'}(\rho h(U,v)\otimes1)$. These calculations take place in the derived sequence categories themselves; applying a functor to these equalities does not require the finite evaluation functors to be faithful.

source.place: Paragraph 2, specified natural mapping-complex maps before limits; explicit pasting of the projection-evaluation word

proof.text:
For $W=X$ set $V=\operatorname{const}K$ and $M(K)=L\rho_X^*V$. Use the precise full-system comparison of [lem-coef-hom-tower-scalar-model]: its first arrow identifies the strict global Hom tower, formed with a K-flat $P\to K$ and a K-injective $I$ of the restricted constant-ring tower, with $Rg_{X*}^RR\mathcal Hom_{R_X^{\mathrm{const}}}(V,\rho_{X*}N)$. Its second arrow uses the inverse scalar internal-Hom isomorphism normalized by evaluation after the scalar-extension unit, then the point-sections comparison. Denote their composite by $\alpha_{K,N}:\mathsf H_N(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}\rho h(M(K),N)$. Both arrows are natural in the derived variables, so
$$\alpha_{K,N}\mathsf H_N(f)=\rho h(M(f),N)\alpha_{K',N}.$$
These are exactly the Hom object and comparison named in [lem-coef-system-projection-evaluation], which specifies
$$\beta_{K,N}=\widetilde\beta_{M(K),N}(\alpha_{K,N}\otimes1),\qquad B_K=\rho b_{M(K)},\quad B(f)=\rho b(M(f)).$$
Substituting the naturality square, applying step 6 with $u=M(f)$, and using tensor bifunctoriality gives
$$\beta_{K,N}(\mathsf H_N(f)\otimes1)=\widetilde\beta_{M(K'),N}(1\otimes B(f))(\alpha_{K',N}\otimes1)=\beta_{K',N}(1\otimes B(f)).$$
No flatness of the quotient ring maps, detection by finite evaluations, trace, or inverse limit is used.
